questions.question: What is a partition of a set $S$?
options: A collection of overlapping subsets whose union is empty.
One event with probability one-half
An ordered list of probabilities only
Nonempty disjoint subsets whose union is $S$.

questions.question: What does a partition do intuitively?
options: It splits a space into cases that may overlap
It splits a space into non-overlapping cases
It picks disjoint cases that may leave some outcomes out
It splits a space into cases that are independent

questions.question: In a partition, how many cases can contain a given outcome?
options: At least two
None
All cases
Exactly one

questions.question: Which condition prevents overlap in a partition?
options: Pairwise intersections are empty
The union is empty
Every subset has probability one
Every subset is a singleton

questions.question: Which condition makes a partition exhaustive?
options: Every subset is empty
Every pair intersects
The union of the subsets is $S$
The subsets all have exactly equal sizes

questions.question: Do disease status and no disease status form a partition of patients?
options: Yes, each patient is in exactly one of the two cases
No, because the two cases have very different sizes
No, because complements are not a partition of the patients
Yes, but only if the disease is rare among the patients

questions.question: Can age groups under thirty, thirty to sixty, and over sixty form a partition if boundaries are defined without overlap?
options: No, because the groups contain different numbers of people
Yes, they can cover each respondent exactly once
No, because a partition must have exactly two blocks
Yes, even if a boundary age belongs to two groups

questions.question: Let $S=\{1,2,3,4\}$. Is $\{\{1,2\},\{3,4\}\}$ a partition?
options: Yes: blocks are nonempty, disjoint, cover $S$
No, because each block must contain a single element
Yes, since a partition only needs disjoint blocks
No, because $S$ itself must be a block

questions.question: Let $S=\{1,2,3\}$. Why is $\{\{1,2\},\{2,3\}\}$ not a partition?
options: The subsets are nonempty
The subsets overlap at $2$
The union contains $S$
There are too many subsets

questions.question: Let $S=\{1,2,3\}$. Why is $\{\{1\},\{2\}\}$ not a partition?
options: The subsets overlap
The union does not cover $3$
The subsets are empty
The collection has more than one subset

questions.question: Why are partitions useful in probability calculations?
options: They make all cases equally likely automatically
They remove the need for events
They force every event to be impossible
They support case-based probability calculations

questions.question: Which probability rule explicitly uses partitions to decompose an event?
options: The law of total probability
The definition of a permutation
The complement notation only
The formula for a factorial

questions.question: Why must partition pieces be nonempty?
options: Empty pieces would make all events independent
Empty pieces force the union to be $S$
Empty pieces do not represent genuine cases
Empty pieces are required by the definition

questions.question: Shipping methods standard, express, and pickup partition orders when what is true?
options: Each order has at least one of these methods
Each order has exactly one of these methods
Each order has at most one of these methods
Each method is used by the same number of orders

questions.question: Which pair forms a partition of a sample space $S$ for any event $A$?
options: $A$ together with itself, a duplicated event
$A$ and $A^c$, if both are nonempty
$A$ and $S$ always
$A\cup S$ and $A\cap S$

questions.question: How is a partition different from an arbitrary collection of events?
options: Non-overlapping and collectively exhaustive.
A partition must contain only one event
A partition's events must have equal probabilities.
A partition cannot be used in probability

questions.question: Why does every outcome belonging to exactly one case matter?
options: It prevents omission and double counting.
It makes all cases have the same probability.
It proves the sample space is infinite
It makes conditional probability undefined
